description: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets collected from either a single data source (represented by blue bars) or two or more data sources (represented by orange bars) across each year from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis displays the years in chronological order, while the vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. For each year, there are two bars: a blue bar indicating datasets from one source and an orange bar indicating datasets from two or more sources. The values for each bar are approximately: 2012 (blue: ~1, orange: ~1), 2013 (blue: ~1, orange: ~0), 2014 (blue: ~1, orange: ~0), 2015 (blue: ~0, orange: ~1), 2016 (blue: ~10, orange: ~2), 2017 (blue: ~20, orange: ~5), 2018 (blue: ~30, orange: ~20), 2019 (blue: ~45, orange: ~20), 2020 (blue: ~85, orange: ~45), 2021 (blue: ~110, orange: ~45), and 2022 (blue: ~30, orange: ~5). The bars are grouped side-by-side for each year, with the blue bar consistently appearing taller than the orange bar in most years except 2018, 2019, and 2020, where the orange bar reaches approximately 20–45 datasets. The chart does not indicate any sorting of the bars by height or value; they are presented chronologically along the x-axis. No bars are visually emphasized or annotated beyond their color-coded representation in the legend.
